## What You'll Learn

Cursor isn't the only AI-native editor on the market. **Windsurf**, built by Codeium, takes a similar approach — VS Code foundations, AI deeply integrated — but with a different philosophy around how the AI agent works. This lesson gives you enough experience to make an informed choice between Cursor and Windsurf in lesson 6-8.

## What Windsurf Is

Windsurf is a code editor by Codeium — a company that has been building AI coding tools since before Cursor existed. Their free VS Code extension (also called Codeium) is used by millions of developers, and Windsurf is their editor product that takes those capabilities further.

**Download:** codeium.com/windsurf — free tier available.

Like Cursor, Windsurf is a VS Code fork. It looks nearly identical to VS Code, imports your settings on first launch, and supports the same extensions. The differences are in how the AI integrates with the editing workflow.

## Cascade — Windsurf's AI Agent

Windsurf's headline feature is **Cascade** — its AI agent system. Cascade is designed around a concept Codeium calls "agentic awareness": the AI doesn't just respond to individual requests, it tracks what you've changed, what errors appeared, and what the current state of the file is — updating its understanding continuously as you work.

**How to use Cascade:**
1. Press **Ctrl+L** to open the Cascade panel on the right side of the editor
2. Choose between **Write** mode (Cascade makes changes to your files) or **Chat** mode (it explains and advises without editing)
3. In Write mode, describe what you want: "Add input validation to the form" — Cascade edits the relevant files and shows you what it changed
4. You can watch it work in real-time: Windsurf shows the edits applying as a live animation

The real-time visual feedback is one of the most distinctive parts of the Windsurf experience. It feels less like submitting a request and more like watching a colleague type.

**The AI editor landscape is moving fast.** Cursor, Windsurf, and the other tools in this category are updated every few weeks. Features that were unique to one editor often appear in the other within months. The goal of lessons 6-6 and 6-7 is not to crown a winner — it's to give you hands-on experience with both approaches so you understand the fundamental design differences and can adapt as the tools evolve.

## Cursor vs. Windsurf — A Quick Comparison

| | Cursor | Windsurf |
|--|--------|----------|
| AI agent name | Composer | Cascade |
| Codebase awareness | Strong — @-file references | Strong — continuous context tracking |
| Free tier | Generous (monthly fast request budget) | Generous (credit-based) |
| AI model | Claude + GPT-4 (your choice) | Codeium's own + Claude |
| Visual feedback | Diff view before applying | Live animation as it edits |
| Privacy mode | Yes (settings) | Yes (settings) |

Neither is clearly superior. Developer communities are split. The right choice depends on which *feels* better to you — which is why you need to try both.

sections.title: Explore Windsurf and Use Cascade
sections.content:
**Step 1 — Download and install Windsurf**
1. Open your browser and go to codeium.com/windsurf
2. Click **Download Windsurf** — select the Windows installer
3. Run the installer, keeping all defaults
4. On first launch, create a free Codeium account (or sign in if you have one)
5. When offered to import from VS Code, accept — your extensions and settings transfer

**Step 2 — Open your project**
1. Click **File → Open Folder** and open `ai-course-projects`
2. Take 2 minutes to orient yourself: the layout is nearly identical to VS Code. Find the Cascade icon in the Activity Bar (it may be labeled with a wave symbol or "Windsurf")

**Step 3 — Use Cascade to modify an existing file**
1. Press **Ctrl+L** to open the Cascade panel
2. Make sure you're in **Write** mode (not Chat)
3. Type this request:
```
Open contact-form.html (created in lesson 6-6). Add a character counter below the message textarea that shows how many characters have been typed out of a 500-character limit. Use plain JavaScript — no libraries.
```
4. Watch Cascade work — observe the live edits appearing in the file
5. When it finishes, open the file in Live Server and test the counter

**Step 4 — Compare the experience to Cursor**
Spend 5 minutes with this checklist:
- [ ] Did Cascade show changes before or after applying them?
- [ ] Was the Cascade panel easier or harder to use than Cursor's Composer?
- [ ] Did Windsurf feel faster, slower, or about the same as Cursor for this task?
- [ ] Did the output code quality seem similar?

**Step 5 — Write your comparison**
In your notes, write 3 sentences comparing Windsurf to Cursor from your personal experience in lessons 6-6 and 6-7. There's no right answer — you're building your own informed opinion.

**Lesson 6-7 complete.** You've now tried both major AI-native editors. You have hands-on experience with Cursor's Composer, Windsurf's Cascade, Copilot Chat, and Continue.dev. In lesson 6-8, you'll synthesize everything from this part into a personal decision about which setup you'll use for the rest of the course.
